steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Melt sugar in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat until liquefied and golden in color. Carefully pour hot syrup into a deep 9-inch round glass baking dish, turning the dish to evenly coat the bottom; set aside.

Beat eggs in a large bowl. Add condensed milk, evaporated milk, and vanilla; beat until smooth. Pour egg mixture on top of caramel in the baking dish; place in a deep roasting pan. Carefully pour in enough hot water to come 1 inch up the sides of the dish.

Bake in the preheated oven until just set with a slight jiggle in the center, about 1 hour, checking after 55 minutes. Keep in mind the flan will continue to set as it cools. Remove from the oven and carefully transfer baking dish to a wire rack; cool to room temperature, then cover with plastic wrap to prevent a skin forming. Refrigerate for 3 hours or up to 3 days.
To serve, run a knife around the edges of the dish; carefully invert onto a rimmed serving plate and let caramel sauce flow over flan.

raw_recipe.headline: Spanish Flan
raw_recipe.description: Spanish flan is a baked custard made with condensed and evaporated milk, eggs, and sugar for a rich, smooth dessert smothered with caramel sauce.

video.description: Discover the art of creating exquisite Spanish Flan with this easy-to-follow video guide. We'll lead you through the steps to master this classic dessert, from caramelizing sugar to achieving the perfect silky custard texture. Impress your family and friends with your culinary skills as you learn to create this delightful treat, which will transport your taste buds to Spain. Don't miss out on this delectable recipe; it's perfect for any special occasion.

review.reviewBody: Best recipe. Simple and the traditional way of making flan. Tips: Keep your baking dish warm/hot in the oven while you make the flan, so that when you do pour your caramel (melted sugar) into it, the caramel doesn't harden as quickly. When melting sugar, be patient and keep the heat LOW because the sugar may brown too dark. Don't fret if you still have small lumps of sugar in the end.. they will desolve when you bake the flan. As for the flan mixture, blend everything in a blender (adding the condensed milk last because its thicker) for the most effective and fastest way of mixing. Also, personally 3 eggs is not enough for me.. I add 5 (known people that add a lot more)... but the egg amount depends on YOUR density peference. Good Luck!

This is the recipe i've always used... but for what here in Mexico we call Chocoflan or Pastel Imposible (in southern mexico.. Impossible Cake)... all you have to do is prepare a chocolate cake mix and pour it over the flan mixture, then bake it on water bath (350 degrees) for 1:20 hours.... I promise you won't regret it :)

This was an awesome recipe! Easy to make and more wonderful to eat! If you are worrying about the carmelized sugar hardening too fast, mix all the ingredients first, and then melt the sugar and swirl in the baking dish. This way, there is no gaps between swirling and pouring your flan mixture into the dish. Also, as a slight variatioin, I added 4oz. (half bar) of cream cheese to the recipe - to give it a firmer texture, since you're only using three eggs. After the flan had cooled completely (about an hour), we could eat it right away instead of torturing ourselves and waiting overnight. You'll be glad you added the cream cheese! Serving suggestion - serve with a scoop of dulce de leche ice cream - you can't go wrong!

I loved this recipe but I gave it 4 out of 5 because the instructions definitely need to be rewritten. I did what other reviewers said to do which was to put it in a water bath.(put flan dish in bigger pan like a baking dish and add boiling water to baking dish before baking) and I took the temp down from 350F to 300F. I also didn’t have evaporated milk so I used half n half which you can use 1:1 ratio to replace evaporated milk so 12 ounces of half n half replaces 12 ounces of evaporated milk. It also has a higher fat content which gave my flan a thick a creamy texture which I loved! I’m definitely going to make this again just keeping the changes I made in how to bake and the temp.

So I attempted the flan first time with 3 eggs and used the hot water bath method for baking, however the flan collapsed (1 star). So I attempted making it again using 6-7 eggs and the hot water bath method and it came out perfect. So this recipe as it may be good for a smaller sized flan, the 3 eggs just is not enough to give it the right density. Picture shown is of the flan made with 6-7 eggs. (5 star) Texture was amazing and it tasted like heaven. Cooked for an hour and in a flan pan purchased from Amazon which has a lid that seals and helps to protect the flan from getting water in it when using the hot water bath method also known as the Bain Marie method. I am not a fan of eggs so I may use a different egg to yolk ratio for the next flan I make. I however was very pleased with how it came out and my husband loved it. I did use the blender as condensed milk is hard to whisk fully with the eggs without making a mess, I also used a mesh strainer to pour the custard into the pan to get out any parts that didn’t mix such as the egg. **When making the Caramel, add some water to the pan and let it sit remembering not to stir too much. Wait for it to turn a nice amber and remove from heat and once it gets a tad darker pour into the pan. I hope this helps anyone whom is new to making flan.

My suggestion to prevent bubbles is to strain the egg/milk mixture several times with a fine mesh sieve. It will give you the smoothest creamiest flan. Also, add 1 additional egg yolk to the recipe. 🤤

I really like this recipe. Though I’ve tweaked it lots of times to perfect it, but it’s the first one that comes out literally PERFECT. Internal temp when it’s finished should be 175✔️ (use a meat thermometer) about 1 hour @350 in a fat water bath. Knock it down to 2 xl eggs instead of what it says. I make mine in a mixer with a paddle attached. Also make sure you melt the sugar all the way till it’s dark and clear. It stays hot long enough for you to coat your ramekins and the flavor is more intense for as dark as you can get it without burning it. After you pour your flans into your ramekins make sure you do a good drop to eliminate any bubbles. An overcooked flan will crack and look like an overcooked egg. Perfect flan will jiggle and be like soft creamy custard with little to no imperfections as you cut into it. If using your ramekins and you are trying to release them, run a sleek knife around the edges and toss it upside down with a good few pats. Should plop out just fine. I wouldn’t serve these hot either. Flipping them too soon can cause them to break even if they are cooked perfectly. Be patient, flan is a custard and it need to SET. give it 15 mins on the counter to cook then let them chill in the fridge for 2-3 hours before you release them. A freakin plus+

The ingredients together is good if you like it very sweet. The cooking instructions on the other hand are not good. For a slightly less sweet version I used 3/4 can of condensed milk, 4 eggs. 2 teaspoons of vanilla and 12 ounces of evaporated milk. I also Baked it at 300F in a water bath. It came it good with these changes

I had never made flan before but I'm a fairly good Baker. I consulted multiple flan recipes and decided after reading the comments to add an additional two eggs to the recipe. After three very long tedious attempts to melt the sugar for caramel with three different outcomes none of which browned at all and twice turned back into powdered sugar I did some research and found a video from America's Test Kitchen. No hands in the microwave and took less than 6 minutes on my first try! You mix a cup of sugar 2 tbsp of corn syrup two tablespoons of water and 8 teaspoon lemon juice in the microwave on high for 5 minutes. Microwaves power vary so watch carefully for the mixture to turn a light brown. Mine took exactly 5 minutes. As you let it sit on the counter for a couple of minutes it will gradually turn brown. Pour the caramel into your dish and continue with the recipe. I will never ever do it differently from now on!!

Writing a review about my experience making this and following advice in the comments. Hope it helps. 1. The hardest part of this was melting the sugar. Don’t do it in a skillet! :) The melting was not happening uniformly. I got impatient and added water, which burned it. Don’t ask me how. Sauce pan worked much better. 2. I used the water bath suggested in the reviews. I don’t know if I was supposed have it covered or not, but I covered it. I had a thin layer of water on the top as a result. My guess is if I cover the dish snuggly without the bath, it would have been fine. Either that or I should leave it uncovered with a water bath. 3. I have a surplus of eggs. I followed the suggestion to 5 instead of 3 to use them up. I liked the result. Just know that each egg added gives you another 1/4 cup of flan mix. Mine went rose up to the brim of the 9.5” pie dish. In summary, I’ll just follow the instructions as written here next time. I WILL make sure to cover the dish securely to avoid (hopefully) the problems some people expressed they had. The recipe is just too simple! I’ll update this review once I make this again.

Made it once, and it turned out delicious, but the texture was a bit off. Still definitely enjoyed and consumed by all. Just made it again and this time I had access to a more temperature stable oven and a deeper water bath. I also decided to filter out the eggie bits that wouldn't go completely into the batter to (hopefully) improve the texture and... Oh my god. It turned out PERFECT. Absolutely delicious. It's such a delicious and easy recipe.

This is life changing. In my whole life, I am most proud of this flan. I’ve always doubted my abilities as a baker, but this is so good I changed my mind. I’ve already 3 more for my family. They were not quite as good as the one in the photo, but everyone loved it. My mom had tears of joy. They were so happy they named their new dog flan.

It's a great dish, but as I make ten at a time at a summer camp, and have a convection oven it took me three times to get it right. In my case I use disposable pans with cooking spray, bake it at 300 degrees on a low fan a water bathwater bath. It's ready in 35 minutes.
Simple and tasty flan.
Absolutely love this recipe! Very simple to follow.
The recipe forgot to include 1/4 C water for melting the sugar. Otherwise, my flan turned out amazing!!

I was scared when I started reading the low ratings on this page after I had finished making the flan BUT it came out amazing! I used cold water for the bath accidently but despite that it came out perfectly. 10/10 would do again.

This recipe is perfect. Super creamy! Family loves it. People keep saying to add more than 3 eggs, but the 3 eggs is perfect because it makes it creamier. Everyone is different so if you want the flan to be more harder and not creamier, then go ahead and add more eggs, but the three eggs is perfect for a creamy flan!

The flan is perfect and only needs the three eggs. It comes out creamy and smooth. I’ve taken this dessert to share with hospital coworkers and several said that this taste better than the ones they’ve eaten at high end restaurants. It’s a keeper/crowd pleaser and easy to make.

Great Flan! Very easy to make and minimal ingrediants! My first attempt followed almost to a T, the one thing i did differently was add small amount of water when making the caramel. I will be using this recipe again although i will be tweaking it just slightly to my liking. All in all, i am very pleased with the results from this and is a great stepping stone to perfecting an amazing flan!
